title: Microsoft logs $3.2B from Anthropic investment, but OpenAI was a mixed bag
slides: Microsoft’s Anthropic bet paid off—why didn’t OpenAI?

thread_text:
1. Microsoft won big.

Anthropic returned $3.2B in under two years — a bet that paid off.

2. OpenAI’s cost spiral.

Microsoft spent billions more than planned on OpenAI, with no comparable return.

3. The contract trap.

Most AI vendor deals lock you in. Your next one needs an exit clause.

4. Cap table red flag.

Check your supplier’s ownership structure before signing — hidden obligations can hurt you.

5. Audit your AI stack.

Pull one prompt from ChatGPT and check if you could switch providers in a week. If not, start now.

instagram.caption:
Microsoft's Anthropic bet returned $3.2B in under two years. OpenAI cost them billions more with no comparable payout.

One AI vendor delivered profits; the other burned cash. The difference? Contract terms and ownership structure—not just tech quality.

If you license AI tools, your deal likely locks you in with no way out. That’s a risk, not a guarantee.

Can you switch providers in a week? If not, check your contract’s exit clause before your next renewal.
